intent: Draw a thin visual line between two sections or items of content, oriented to match how they are laid out.
typical_uses: A horizontal rule between stacked sections of a page or panel
A vertical rule between items in a horizontal toolbar

dont_use_when.situation: Inside a kit container that ships its own separator part (a menu or select popup, a combobox or command list, a button group, a sidebar)

instead.target: that container's own separator part, for example DropdownMenuSeparator or SelectSeparator
instead.note: Each of those containers exports a separator part styled for its own layout (a popup's list bleeds it into the popup's padding); there are several, so no single reference names them all.

dont_use_when.situation: Marking the edge of a framed region

instead.target: the container's own border, for example Card
the surrounding layout's own CSS gap or margin
instead.note: Separator always renders a visible line; it is not a spacer, and this kit ships no spacer component. Reserve empty space with layout, not with a divider made to look invisible.

invariants.text: The rendered div carries role="separator" unless the consumer passes its own role, with data-orientation and aria-orientation both set to the orientation prop's resolved value - horizontal when the prop is omitted, since Base UI defaults it internally rather than through a schema-visible default. The kit's CSS switches the div's width and height off data-orientation.

Base UI's Separator has no separate decorative flag; role="separator" and aria-orientation are Base UI's own defaults, merged before the consumer's own props, so a consumer's own aria-hidden="true" always wins on the DOM node and removes the element from the accessibility tree entirely - the role and aria-orientation stay on the node but stop mattering once aria-hidden takes effect. role="none" alone does not achieve the same result: aria-orientation stays set regardless of role, and aria-orientation on a role that does not permit it is an aria-allowed-attr violation.

The vertical orientation is drawn with align-self: stretch, which only has an effect inside a flex or grid parent with a real cross-axis size. In a plain block parent, or in a flex row whose other items are themselves all zero-height, the divider collapses to zero height regardless of the parent's own align-items setting.

anti_patterns.dont: Expect a vertical separator to render inside a plain block parent, or a flex row whose other items are themselves zero-height
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give the parent a real flex or grid cross-axis size (or set a height on the Separator directly) - align-self:stretch has nothing to stretch into otherwise

anti_patterns.dont: Restyle the divider through an inline style prop for a brand or theme change
anti_patterns.do_instead: Change the kit's --border theme token instead - brand changes belong in tokens, not per-instance overrides

a11y.by: Base UI's own Separator primitive (role="separator", data-orientation and aria-orientation stamped from the orientation prop, elementProps merged last so a consumer's own aria-hidden always wins) plus separator.test.tsx's own role/aria-orientation/data-orientation assertions and its check that queryByRole('separator') returns null once aria-hidden="true" is set

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through separator.module.css, not through this.

good.title: Vertical, inside a flex row with a real cross-axis height
good.code: Bold Italic

bad.title: Used inside a DropdownMenuContent list
bad.why: Separator carries no popup-scoped styling (no bleed margin into the popup's padding); DropdownMenuSeparator wraps the same primitive with that styling applied.

bad.title: A vertical separator placed in a plain block parent
bad.why: align-self: stretch has no flex or grid context to act in here, so the divider collapses to zero height and renders nothing visible - make the parent display:flex (or grid), or give the Separator its own height.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies.
